summary: Data Science With Sam EP47 adds a privacy-first AI product branch: Kind/Synsira makes local files, prompt exposure, RAG grounding, refusal behavior, and digital-sovereignty control part of product-market trust rather than only model quality. The All-In source adds an AI-infrastructure and SaaS reset branch: SpaceX/Starlink/Starship capacity claims, compute price risk, data-center debt, Airtable's sale to Bending Spoons, Hyper Agent, product-led growth, liquidation preferences, and private-equity owner fit connect AI-era business value to layer economics and balance-sheet risk; the episode's figures and deal interpretations remain source-scoped. The burger/lemon source adds an operating-fit consumer branch: burgers, Coach, Moutai, domestic yellow lemons, and discount retail show that growth under cautious demand depends on store format, channel discipline, supply-demand timing, and whether low prices are structural or merely opportunistic. The Flock source adds a govtech/public-safety market branch: adoption of sensor infrastructure depends on legitimacy, retention defaults, auditability, local approval, and police-trust risk as much as product utility. The Korea development source adds a national-industrial version of the corpus pattern: entrepreneurs, subsidies, and market openings become durable only when export competition, transferable know-how, and property protection discipline them. South Korea turns strategic support into development through land-reform equality, export discipline, and firm upgrading; Bangladesh shows garment capability moving through people, quotas, and Daewoo/Desh training while still facing safety and ladder-climbing limits; North Korea shows market energy remaining confiscation-prone when donju entrepreneurship lacks secure rights. The Intelligence source adds a cross-domain caution: orexin drugs, Japanese startups, and procrastination interventions all need grounded adoption gates before hype becomes durable value; the episode keeps the GLP-1 analogy, Japan market reform, and behavioral intervention evidence qualified rather than settled. The Whatnot source adds a live-commerce version: [[Whatnot]] did not make Western livestream retail work generically, but matched [[MarketplaceLiveCommerce]] to collectible auctions, status rewards, and card-break uncertainty while keeping overspending and gambling-adjacent risk source-scoped. Its side items add Geely governance, ByteDance/MPA rights protection, Proya/Ulta outbound beauty retail, and Damai designer-toy IP as distribution or control advantages that still need operating proof. The business and market sources repeatedly separate attention and formal ownership from durable value: customer pull, payment proof, distribution, operating capacity, local decision rights, trust, supply-chain leverage, verification, logistics security, valuation discipline, and repeat demand determine whether an attractive idea survives contact with real markets. Templafy adds an enterprise SaaS version of that pattern: pre-product selling can be useful when budget, timing, proof criteria, and rollout consequences are explicit, and technology resets can force product rebuilds before old moats carry forward. Unitree adds a robotics-public-market version of that pattern: a listing surge and low-cost robot platform are not enough without buyers, tasks, repeat purchase, scene-specific ROI, and a defensible split between existing business value and future humanoid option value. Huawei's automotive ecosystem adds an alliance-platform version: a company may avoid formal car manufacturing while still shaping products, channels, service standards, brands, and supplier architecture through Hongmeng Zhixing, the smart selection model, channel migration, and Yinwang. Sell Me a Sasquatch adds a mass-retail version: a playable economics game still needed line-review approval, audience proof, planogram and shelf confidence, a $19.99 price frame, licensed-risk allocation, packaging decisions, and factory deadlines before it could appear at Target and Walmart. The August 21 Marketplace Tech Bytes source adds a physical-operations version: AI data-center growth can make cargo theft, export-control leakage, cooling parts, cabling, and drone-delivery acceptance into market constraints rather than background infrastructure. The AI, SaaS, CPG, restaurant, finance, creator, sports, banking, insurance, prediction-market, automotive, robotics, governance, and development sources all preserve the same distinction between capability or attention and the systems that make value repeatable. Hanji 1009 remains a source-scoped political analogy in which Cao Cao's reputation for protecting a surrendered rival preserves future access to talent. The Food Republic coffee-bean source adds a restaurant-retail version: consumer meal demand persists, but the organizing model shifts away from Food Republic-style second-landlord stall aggregation toward chain brands, direct mall leasing, delivery-platform economics, platform canteens, supermarket prepared meals, and scene-led or higher-end food-market operators; Carlsberg adds a smaller beverage-portfolio example where alcohol-free beer and soft drinks hedge traditional category weakness. Hanji 932 enters this topic only as a source-scoped fiscal-governance analogy: fee-burdened office works like a debt-recovery channel, not a modern market case.
